tool.name: list_ad_accounts
tool.title: List Ad Accounts
tool.description:
Discover and list all Meta ad accounts the user can access — start here.

This is the entry point for every session. Call this FIRST to find available
ad accounts and get the ad_account_id values required by all other tools.

Returns each account's name, numeric ID, platform type, business name,
currency, data_synced / landed / sync_state, and pixel summary (id, name,
last_fired_time, and hosts for each pixel on the account). Use the hosts
to identify which pixel belongs to which website/business.

data_synced=false means the account's first Meta sync has not completed:
history older than 90 days is still syncing. While live_reads_enabled is
true, every read tool then answers live from Meta and is complete for the
last 90 days and for current entities — do not wait for data_synced to
analyse recent performance. A question the live path cannot answer
(history beyond 90 days, too many entities) comes back as
status='not_yet_landed' with the sync_state; sync_state.streams_done /
streams_total is what to relay when the user asks how far along the sync
is. While live_reads_enabled is false such accounts read the partial
synced copy, as before.

After listing accounts, read the resource adadvisor://account/{ad_account_id}/context
to get the numbers this business's ads are judged by (break-even ROAS and AOV
for a sales business, break-even and target cost per lead for a leads
business, plus the daily budget cap) and the AI-generated business research
report.

outputSchema.description: Response from list_ad_accounts.

live_reads_enabled.description: Environment switch. True: accounts whose first sync has not completed are read live from Meta (90-day window). False: such accounts read the partial synced copy, as before.

items.description: One ad account row from list_ad_accounts.

is_active.description: Whether the account is connected and active.

data_synced.description: False until the account's first Meta sync has completed in full. While false (and live_reads_enabled is true) reads are served live from Meta and are complete for the last 90 days and current entities; only older history is still syncing.

landed.description: The switch the data service routes on: true = every read comes from the synced copy; false = the first sync is still running. Null for non-Meta accounts or when the sync record is unreadable.

sync_state.description: Progress of the first sync (Meta accounts): landed, phase (initial | catchup | landed | failed), streams {name: pending | running | completed | failed}, streams_done / streams_total, insights_chunks {done, total}, started_at, landed_at, failed_at. Relay streams_done/streams_total when the user asks how far along the sync is.

items.description: Pixel summary attached to an ad account.

id.description: Pixel ID.

last_fired_time.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last firing.

hosts.description: Domains the pixel fires on, sorted by hit count.

tool.name: list_pages
tool.title: List Pages
tool.description:
List Facebook Pages reachable for advertising from this ad account.

Returns each page's id, name, the connecting user's Page-role tasks
(e.g. ADVERTISE, MANAGE, ANALYZE), and can_advertise. is_default marks
the page create_lead_form uses when page_id is omitted.

Pages are the union of the ad account's promote_pages edge and the user's
/me/accounts, deduped (the same source the app's page picker uses). Prefer
can_advertise=true pages. tasks are joined from /me/accounts because the
promote_pages edge does not return tasks.

Use this to:
- Pin a specific page_id on create_lead_form when the account has more than one page.
- Check whether the connecting user has the ADVERTISE task on the page.

Note: an empty tasks list is advisory, not a hard block — a system-user
or granular-scope grant (pages_manage_ads / leads_retrieval) can still
let create_ad / create_lead_form succeed even when tasks is empty. Prefer
attempting the real mutation over refusing on an empty tasks list.

Calls Meta directly — pages are not ingested into the tenant DB.

items.description: One Page row from list_pages.

tasks.description: The connecting user's Page-role tasks (from /me/accounts), e.g. ADVERTISE, MANAGE, ANALYZE. Empty means the user holds no Page role on it — advisory only, not a hard block (a granular-scope or system-user grant can still allow ad/form creation).

can_advertise.description: True if this Page is advertisable by this ad account — it is in the account's promote_pages OR the user holds the ADVERTISE task on it.

is_default.description: True for the page used by create_lead_form when page_id is omitted.

tool.name: list_adsets
tool.title: List Ad Sets
tool.description:
List ad sets — show targeting, budgets, and optimization config.

Use this to see what ad sets exist, review targeting and setup, or
answer "what ad sets are in this campaign?" questions.

Returns: id, name, campaign_id, status, targeting, daily_budget,
lifetime_budget, budget_remaining, bid_amount, bid_strategy,
optimization_goal, destination_type, billing_event, promoted_object,
start_time / end_time, pacing_type, adset_schedule,
learning_stage_info, and CBO ad-set-level spend controls
(daily_min_spend_target, daily_spend_cap, lifetime_min_spend_target,
lifetime_spend_cap). The spend controls populate from the 30-min
refresh — null on rows synced before the field landed.

Delivery schedule (dayparting): adset_schedule is a list of blocks
{days: ["Mon", ...], start: "HH:MM", end: "HH:MM", timezone_type} —
the ad set delivers ONLY inside them (end "24:00" = end of day;
timezone_type USER = the viewer's time zone, ADVERTISER = the ad
account's). [] means no dayparting. pacing_type ["day_parting"] says
the same thing from the synced copy. A $0 day that falls outside the
schedule (e.g. a Friday for a Mon–Thu schedule) is the schedule
working, NOT a delivery stop — check this before calling spend loss.
Meta keeps dayparting on the ad set even when Ads Manager shows it as
a campaign setting ("campaign_schedule" in the change log).

learning_stage_info: {status, conversions, last_sig_edit_time,
attribution_windows}. status LEARNING = still in the learning phase,
SUCCESS = exited learning, FAIL = "Learning limited". null = Meta
reports no learning stage for this ad set (e.g. not delivering). Meta
does not expose the reasons behind "Learning limited".

adset_schedule and learning_stage_info are read live from Meta at
call time (the synced copy does not hold them). When that read fails
they are null on every row and live_fields_unavailable says why — do
not read those nulls as "no schedule" or "not learning".

For lead generation, destination_type + promoted_object are what tell
you where the leads actually go: ON_AD = instant form on the ad itself
(promoted_object.page_id), WEBSITE = an offsite landing page
(promoted_object.pixel_id + custom_event_type=LEAD), MESSENGER /
INSTAGRAM_DIRECT / WHATSAPP = a messaging thread, PHONE_CALL = a call.
destination_type is null on ad sets last synced before it was
ingested — re-sync to populate it.

tool.description:
List ads — show which creatives are running and their setup.

Use this to see what ads exist, review creative details, or answer
"what ads are in this ad set/campaign?" questions.

Returns: id, name, campaign_id, adset_id, status, creative, tracking_specs,
issues_info, ad_review_feedback.

Why an ad is not delivering: for ads whose status is WITH_ISSUES,
DISAPPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW or PENDING_BILLING_INFO, issues_info is
Meta's list of delivery issues [{error_code, error_summary,
error_message, error_type, level}] and ad_review_feedback is the
review result ({"global": {"<policy>": "<explanation>"}} when an ad is
rejected). Both are read live from Meta at call time. For every other
status they are null — not read, because Meta reports nothing for an
ad that is delivering normally or paused. If the live read fails they
are null and live_fields_unavailable says why.

`creative` is a REFERENCE — normally just {"id": "..."} — not the creative
itself. To see what the ad actually runs (its copy, media, and any
lead_gen_form_id), take creative.id and call:
  list_creatives(account_id, creative_ids=['<creative.id>'])

When has_more is true, call again with offset=next_offset to fetch the next page.

Does NOT include performance metrics — use get_performance for that.

tool.title: Get Performance
tool.description:
Get performance metrics — how are my campaigns/ads doing?

Use this to compare entities, find top or bottom performers, check
spend and ROAS, or get an overview of account performance.

Each row includes the ad set's primary Result (Meta Ads Manager's
KPI column): result_count, result_value, cost_per_result, plus
result_action_type (raw Meta event) and conversion_result_name
(humanized label, e.g. "Purchase", "Subscribe", "Lead"). PREFER
these when reporting performance — they reflect what the user sees
in Ads Manager. Legacy purchases / leads / revenue / cpa remain for
backward compat but will be 0 on Subscribe / Lead / custom-conversion
campaigns where result_count is the real KPI.

For mixed-KPI entities (has_multiple_conversions=True — common on
campaigns/creatives whose child adsets optimize for different goals),
response_format='full' additionally returns kpi_breakdown: an array
of per-KPI buckets {action_type, conversion_result_name, result_count,
result_value, cost_per_result, spend} sorted by result_count DESC.
Use it to answer "which KPI is driving this campaign" without a
follow-up call.

Also returns: id, name, status, objective, objective_label, spend,
roas, cpl, cpc, cpm, ctr, clicks, impressions, link_clicks,
landing_page_views, daily_budget, days_active,

pixel funnel ON the site and start at ViewContent — do not use a

minutes and may lag behind real-time. Before that (data_synced=false

provenance — and is complete for the last 90 days and current
entities; days_active is null until the sync completes, and a window
reaching further back than 90 days, or include_lead_breakdown,
returns status='not_yet_landed' with the sync_state instead of rows.

tool.name: get_timeseries
tool.title: Get Timeseries
tool.description:
Get daily trend data — spot performance shifts day over day.

Use this to see how a campaign, ad set, or ad is trending, detect when
a performance change started, or compare day-over-day patterns.

Defaults: the trailing 28 days ending yesterday (or ending end_date)
and response_format='concise'. Large answers get truncated by the
calling agent (an agent harness typically keeps ~16,000 characters of
one tool result, and the per-day rows at the end are what is lost): a
'full' series over more than ~2 weeks, or a campaign whose days carry
a kpi_breakdown, can exceed that. Stay concise, narrow start_date /
end_date, and ask for 'full' only for the few days you need.

A $0 day is not by itself a delivery stop: an ad set with dayparting
(list_adsets → adset_schedule) spends nothing on its off-schedule days.

Each day includes the entity's primary Result (Meta Ads Manager's
KPI column): result_count, result_value, cost_per_result, plus
result_action_type (raw Meta event) and conversion_result_name
(humanized label). PREFER these when reporting trends — they reflect
what the user sees in Ads Manager. Legacy purchases / leads /
revenue / cpa remain for backward compat but will be 0 on Subscribe
/ Lead / custom-conversion entities where result_count is the real
KPI.

When a day spans multiple KPIs (has_multiple_conversions=True on
that day — rare for adsets/ads, common on campaign-level queries),
response_format='full' additionally returns kpi_breakdown for that
day: an array of per-KPI buckets sorted by result_count DESC. Use
it to see the per-KPI split rather than a single aggregated Result.

Also returns per day: spend, roas, cpl, cpc, cpm, ctr, clicks,
impressions, link_clicks, landing_page_views, the pixel funnel
conversion rates and frequency ('full' only for the last two).
landing_page_views ÷ link_clicks is the click-to-site rate; the
vc_to_atc_pct / atc_to_ic_pct / ic_to_purchase_pct rates are the
on-site pixel funnel and start at ViewContent, not at the click.

For account-level totals, use get_performance at campaign level instead.
Once the account's first sync has completed, data refreshes every 30
minutes and may lag behind real-time; before that the series is read
live from Meta (see provenance) and a start_date older than 90 days
returns status='not_yet_landed' with the sync_state instead of days.

entity_id.description: The specific campaign, ad set, or ad ID (from list_campaigns, list_adsets, list_ads, or get_performance). Must NOT be the account ID.

start_date.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 27 days before end_date — a trailing 28-day window.

response_format.description: Default 'concise': per day date_start, day_of_week, spend, impressions, cpm, clicks, ctr, link_clicks, landing_page_views, result_count, cost_per_result, conversion_result_name, result_action_type, roas, revenue, purchases, leads, cpa. 'full' adds every field (reach-based frequency, cpc, cpl, aov, the pixel funnel counts and rates, kpi_breakdown) and is several times larger — use it only over a narrow date range.

tool.name: change_entity_status
tool.title: Change Entity Status
tool.description:
Pause or resume one or more Meta campaigns, ad sets, or ads. Takes effect immediately.

Live mutation — entities stop or start delivering on Meta right away.
Idempotent: pausing an already-paused entity (or resuming an already-active
entity) succeeds without error.

Batch behavior: each entity is processed independently. A failure on one
entity does not abort the others — inspect the per-item ``status`` in
the returned ``results`` list.

All changes are tracked with before/after state snapshots for auditability.
Confirm current status with list_campaigns, list_adsets, or list_ads first.

account_id.description: Ad account ID. Must match the account each entity_id lives under — passing an entity_id from a different account causes Meta to return code 100 (parameter error). When unsure, look the IDs up via list_campaigns / list_adsets / list_ads first.

entity_ids.description: One or more entity IDs to update (from list_campaigns, list_adsets, list_ads, or get_performance — never invent IDs). All IDs must be of the same entity_type. Pass a list with one element for a single update, or many elements to apply the same action to all of them in one call.

action.description: 'pause' stops delivery (sets PAUSED), 'resume' reactivates (sets ACTIVE). For ARCHIVED/DELETED, use update_entity.

agent_intent.description: OPTIONAL free-text describing why the agent is making this change (e.g. 'pausing fatigued ads with CTR < 0.5%'). Logged for telemetry.

outputSchema.description:
Result of pausing or resuming entities.

`status='success'` means every item succeeded. `status='partial'` means
some failed (inspect each `results[i].status`).

next_steps.description: Recommended follow-up tool call(s) for the LLM. Required on every successful mutation per CLAUDE.md; left Optional here because some tools (e.g. update_entity) currently omit it.

results.description: Per-entity results — one entry per requested entity_id.

items.description: Per-entity result inside a batch mutation response.

error.description: Populated when status='error' — human-readable failure reason.

tool.name: change_entity_budget
tool.title: Change Entity Budget
tool.description:
Update the budget of a Meta campaign or ad set. Takes effect immediately.

Provide exactly one of daily_budget or lifetime_budget in the account's currency
(e.g. 50.00 = $50/day). You cannot switch between budget types — the entity must
already use the type you are updating. Check with list_campaigns or list_adsets first.

Safety: changes >2× the current value (in either direction) are rejected unless
force=True. This prevents an LLM hallucinating a 10× budget increase.

Idempotent: setting the same budget again succeeds without error.
All changes are tracked with before/after state snapshots for auditability.

account_id.description: Ad account ID. Must be the account where entity_id lives — Meta returns code 100 (parameter error) on a mismatch. Check via list_campaigns or list_adsets if you're not sure.

entity_type.description: 'campaign' or 'adset'. Ads do not have budgets.

entity_id.description: The campaign or ad set ID (from list_campaigns, list_adsets, or get_performance — never invent IDs)

lifetime_budget.description: New lifetime budget in account currency (e.g. 500.00 = $500 total). Provide this OR daily_budget, not both.

force.description: Bypass the >100% delta guardrail. By default, budget changes of more than 2× the current value (in either direction) are rejected to prevent accidental runaway edits. Set True to intentionally apply a large change.

agent_intent.description: OPTIONAL free-text describing why the agent is changing this budget (e.g. 'doubling the winning ad set after 3-day soak'). Logged for telemetry.

state_after.description: Entity state snapshot after the change (shape varies by entity type).

tool.name: update_entity
tool.title: Update Entity Fields
tool.description:
Patch arbitrary fields on a Meta campaign, ad set, or ad. Idempotent.

Long-tail edit tool. Use the dedicated change_entity_status / change_entity_budget
tools for the hot paths — they are safer and have richer error messages.
Each field of EntityFieldsPatch documents which entity_type(s) it applies to.

Live mutation — changes apply immediately on Meta. State before/after is
captured for audit. NOT for editing targeting (use update_adset_targeting).

account_id.description: Ad account ID. The account where entity_id lives — Meta returns code 100 (parameter error) if entity_id belongs to a different account. Look up via list_campaigns, list_adsets, or list_ads when uncertain.

entity_type.description: The type of entity to patch.

entity_id.description: ID of the entity to patch (from list_campaigns, list_adsets, or list_ads — never invent IDs).

fields.description:
Object whose set fields are applied to the entity. Each field in EntityFieldsPatch lists which entity_type(s) it applies to; passing a field that doesn't apply to the chosen entity_type returns a validation error.
Currency fields (daily_budget, lifetime_budget, spend_cap, bid_amount) are in account currency — converted server-side.

name.description: Display name. Applies to: campaign, adset, ad.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Applies to: campaign, adset, ad. PAUSED, ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DELETED. For pause/resume prefer change_entity_status.

adlabels.description: Meta ad labels for cross-entity tagging/analytics, e.g. [{'name': 'BlackFriday2026'}]. Applies to: campaign, ad.

bid_strategy.description: Bid strategy. Applies to: campaign, adset.

start_time.description: ISO datetime, e.g. '2026-01-15T00:00:00-0500'. Applies to: campaign, adset.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in account currency (e.g. 50.0 = $50/day). Applies to: campaign, adset. Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. Prefer change_entity_budget for safer edits.

lifetime_budget.description: Lifetime budget in account currency. Applies to: campaign, adset. Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Prefer change_entity_budget.

stop_time.description: ISO datetime for campaign end. Applies to: campaign.

special_ad_categories.description: Special ad categories. Allowed: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES (replaces CREDIT from Jan 14 2025), ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS. Use ['NONE'] for standard ads. Pair with special_ad_category_country whenever a non-NONE value is supplied. Applies to: campaign.

special_ad_category_country.description: ISO country codes scoping special_ad_categories (e.g. ['CA', 'GB']). Required by Meta whenever special_ad_categories contains a non-NONE value. Applies to: campaign.

spend_cap.description: Lifetime spend ceiling in account currency (e.g. 5000.0 = $5,000 max). Pass 0 to REMOVE an existing spend cap (Meta's documented remove-cap value). Applies to: campaign.

billing_event.description: Billing event (IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, THRUPLAY). Applies to: adset.

optimization_goal.description: Optimization goal. Meta rejects this on an ad set whose campaign has already published — duplicate the ad set and change it on the copy. Applies to: adset.

anyOf.description:
Conversion tracking config for an ad set.

tool.name: create_campaign
tool.title: Create Campaign(s)
tool.description:
Create one or more Meta ad campaigns. NOT idempotent — each call creates new campaigns.

All campaigns are created as PAUSED. After creation, add ad sets with
create_adset, then activate with change_entity_status(action='resume').

For most use cases, use objective=OUTCOME_SALES with budget at the
campaign level and LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP bid strategy.

promoted_object goes on the AD SET, not here — the only exception is
OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION, where Meta requires it at campaign level for
iOS 14+. Setting it here for OUTCOME_LEADS or OUTCOME_SALES is
rejected with subcode 1815023. For a lead campaign, set
promoted_object={'page_id': ...} on create_adset instead (or
{'pixel_id': ..., 'custom_event_type': 'LEAD'} for website leads).

Set spend_cap as a safety ceiling whenever this is called by an agent.

account_id.description: Ad account ID where the new campaign(s) will live. Verify the account is reachable via list_ad_accounts first.

campaigns.description: Array of campaign specs to create. Required: objective. Optional: name (auto-generated if omitted), budgets, bid_strategy, schedule, special_ad_categories, promoted_object (ONLY for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION — for OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES it belongs on the ad set), spend_cap (lifetime ceiling), is_skadnetwork_attribution (iOS), source_campaign_id, adlabels.

items.description: Specification for creating a single Meta campaign.

name.description: Campaign name. Omit to auto-generate a structured name: ADADVISOR || CBO/ABO || BOF/MOF/TOF || {strategy} || {business} || {date}.

strategy_label.description: Short 1-2 word label for the campaign strategy, used in auto-generated names. Examples: 'Prospecting', 'Retargeting', 'Scaling', 'Conversions'. Defaults to 'Prospecting' if name is omitted.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in account currency (e.g. 50.0 = $50/day). Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. Budget can be set at campaign OR adset level, not both.

lifetime_budget.description: Lifetime budget in account currency. Requires stop_time. Mutually exclusive with daily_budget.

bid_strategy.description: Bid strategy. Omitted on a campaign that carries a budget (daily_budget or lifetime_budget), the api sends LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (auto-bid) explicitly — because Meta itself would otherwise assign LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, and every ad set under the campaign would then fail with subcode 1815857 for lack of a bid_amount. COST_CAP and LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP need a bid_amount on the AD SET (cap values are set there, not here). A campaign with no budget sets no strategy: each ABO ad set owns its own.

special_ad_categories.description: Special ad categories. Allowed values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES (replaces the legacy CREDIT input from Jan 14 2025), ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS. Use ['NONE'] or omit for standard ads. When any value other than NONE is supplied, special_ad_category_country becomes required.

start_time.description: ISO datetime for campaign start, e.g. '2025-01-15T00:00:00-0500'

stop_time.description: ISO datetime for campaign end. Required with lifetime_budget.

spend_cap.description: Lifetime spend ceiling in account currency (e.g. 5000.0 = $5,000 max total). Hard cap — Meta stops delivery when reached. Acts as a safety rail; recommended whenever an automated agent is creating campaigns.

anyOf.description:
Conversion tracking config for an ad set.

Auto-resolved for OUTCOME_SALES campaigns if omitted (picks account pixel + PURCHASE).

pixel_id.description: Meta pixel ID for conversion tracking

object_store_url.description: App Store / Google Play URL (required with application_id for app promotion)

promoted_object.description:
Conversion tracking config at the CAMPAIGN level. Meta requires this only for iOS 14+ app promotion — set application_id + object_store_url on OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION.
Do NOT set it for OUTCOME_LEADS or OUTCOME_SALES: those belong on the AD SET (AdSetSpec.promoted_object), and putting one here is rejected with subcode 1815023.

special_ad_category_country.description: ISO country codes scoping the special_ad_categories. Required by Meta for international housing/credit/employment campaigns outside the US (e.g. ['CA', 'GB']). Omit for US-only or non-special campaigns.

is_skadnetwork_attribution.description: Set True for iOS app campaigns that must use Apple's SKAdNetwork attribution (post-iOS 14.5). Required for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION targeting iOS.

source_campaign_id.description: Existing campaign ID whose settings to copy as the template for the new campaign. Different from duplicate_campaign — that copies the live entity AND its children; this only seeds the campaign-level config.

adlabels.description: Optional Meta ad labels for cross-campaign tagging/analytics rollups. JSON array of label specs, e.g. [{'name': 'BlackFriday2026'}].

is_adset_budget_sharing_enabled.description: Ad set budget sharing (ABS). Only meaningful when budget is at the ad set level (no daily_budget / lifetime_budget on this spec). Required by Meta v24+ for ABO campaigns: pass True to let ad sets share up to 20% of budget with siblings, False to keep each ad set's budget isolated. Omit when setting a campaign-level budget (CBO).

agent_intent.description: OPTIONAL free-text describing why the agent is creating these campaigns (e.g. 'Q2 retargeting test for cart abandoners'). Logged for telemetry.

outputSchema.description:
Result of create_campaign — N campaigns created (all PAUSED).

`status='success'` means every spec succeeded. `status='partial'` means
some specs failed (inspect the per-item entries in `errors`).

next_steps.description: Recommended follow-up tool call(s) for the LLM. Required on every successful mutation per CLAUDE.md; left Optional here because some tools (e.g. update_entity) currently omit it.

index.description: Position of this spec in the input array.

status.description: Always PAUSED — Meta requires explicit activation via change_entity_status.

state_after.description: Snapshot of the new campaign as Meta returned it.

errors.description: Per-item failure records (name + format_tool_error keys). Present when error_count > 0.

tool.name: create_adset
tool.title: Create Ad Set(s)
tool.description:
Create one or more Meta ad sets. NOT idempotent — each call creates new ad sets.

All ad sets are created as PAUSED. The targeting spec is assembled
server-side from flat inputs (same format as update_adset_targeting)
and validated via /reachestimate before creation.

The campaign_id can be any existing campaign in the account — use
list_campaigns to find one, or create_campaign to make a new one.

Workflow (new campaign):
1. create_campaign(...) to get a campaign_id
2. search_targeting(search_type='interests', query='...') to find IDs
3. create_adset(adsets=[{campaign_id, countries, interests, ...}])
4. change_entity_status(action='resume') to activate

Workflow (existing campaign):
1. list_campaigns to find the campaign_id
2. create_adset(adsets=[{campaign_id, countries, interests, ...}])
3. change_entity_status(action='resume') to activate

Pixel / promoted_object: For OUTCOME_SALES campaigns, the promoted_object
(pixel + conversion event) is auto-resolved if omitted — but it picks the
first pixel on the account, which may not be correct if the account has
multiple pixels for different sites. Call get_pixel_health or check the
pixels array from list_ad_accounts to identify the right pixel by its hosts,
then pass it explicitly via promoted_object={pixel_id, custom_event_type}.

advantage_audience.description: Enable Advantage+ audience expansion (Meta's ML broadens targeting beyond your spec). DEFAULTS TO TRUE — recommended for most cases. Set to False when you need a hard demographic cap (age_max<65, narrow gender) or any constraint Meta must respect exactly. Meta rejects advantage_audience=True combined with age_max<65. When True, any custom audiences / lookalikes / detailed targeting you pass are automatically submitted as Advantage+ *signals* (the 'relaxed setup'); they cannot be hard controls while Advantage+ is on (Meta rejects that as subcode 1359202) — set False to use them as controls.

publisher_platforms.description: Restrict which platforms the ad set may deliver on. Omit for Advantage+ placements (recommended — Meta optimizes across all of them). Call ads REQUIRE ['facebook'].

facebook_positions.description: Facebook surfaces, e.g. ['feed','video_feeds','story','reels', 'marketplace','search']. Requires 'facebook' in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Instagram surfaces, e.g. ['stream','story','reels','explore']. Requires 'instagram' in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Audience Network surfaces, e.g. ['classic','rewarded_video']. Requires 'audience_network' in publisher_platforms.

device_platforms.description: Device types. Omit for both. Call ads REQUIRE ['mobile'] — a desktop user cannot place a phone call from an ad.

optimization_goal.description:
Optimization goal. Defaults to OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS. Use CONVERSATIONS for messaging-destination ad sets (destination_type=WHATSAPP / MESSENGER / INSTAGRAM_DIRECT) — Meta requires it on Click-to-Messenger / Click-to-WhatsApp / Click-to-Instagram / Click-to-MultiDestination ad sets.
Lead generation:
- LEAD_GENERATION optimizes for lead VOLUME. Pair with destination_type=ON_AD and promoted_object={page_id}.
- QUALITY_LEAD optimizes for lead QUALITY (Conversion Leads). Needs destination_type=ON_AD or MESSENGER and promoted_object={page_id}, and only works once the advertiser sends lead-stage events back via the Conversions API — without that CRM feedback Meta has no quality signal to optimize on.
- QUALITY_CALL optimizes for call quality on call ads (destination_type=PHONE_CALL, promoted_object={page_id}).
Meta does NOT allow changing optimization_goal on a campaign that has already published; duplicate the ad set and change it on the copy instead.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in account currency. Only if campaign has NO campaign-level budget.

lifetime_budget.description: Lifetime budget in account currency. Requires end_time.

daily_min_spend_target.description: CBO only: minimum daily spend Meta will try to allocate to this ad set, in account currency. Requires the parent campaign to own a daily_budget (do not pair with an ad-set-level daily_budget). Best-effort, not a hard floor. Note: duplicate_adset(deep_copy=True) carries this over from the source ad set — if the sum of sibling floors exceeds the campaign budget, Meta blocks activation with subcode 1885648. Pass 0 to clear the inherited floor.

daily_spend_cap.description: CBO only: daily spend ceiling for this ad set, in account currency. Requires the parent campaign to own a daily_budget. Meta enforces a minimum of $1 — passing 0 fails with subcode 1885056 ('maximum spend limit must be at least $1.00'). To remove an existing cap, clear it in Ads Manager.

lifetime_min_spend_target.description: CBO only: minimum lifetime spend Meta will try to allocate to this ad set, in account currency. Requires the parent campaign to own a lifetime_budget. Best-effort, not a hard floor. Pass 0 to clear.

lifetime_spend_cap.description: CBO only: lifetime spend ceiling for this ad set, in account currency. Requires the parent campaign to own a lifetime_budget. Meta enforces a minimum (subcode 1885056) — passing 0 will be rejected. To remove an existing cap, clear it in Ads Manager.

bid_strategy.description: Bid strategy. On an ad set that owns its own budget (ABO), omitting it defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (auto-bid) — or to LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP when a bid_amount is supplied. A CBO ad set (no ad-set budget; the campaign holds it) sets none and inherits the campaign's strategy. COST_CAP requires bid_amount (cost-per-result goal). LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP requires bid_amount (max bid per auction). LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS requires roas_average_floor and optimization_goal=VALUE.

bid_amount.description: For COST_CAP: the cost-per-result goal in account currency (e.g. 10.0 = $10/result). For LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP: the max bid per auction in account currency. Do NOT set with LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (use roas_average_floor instead).

roas_average_floor.description: Minimum ROAS floor for LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS strategy. Expressed as a multiplier: 1.5 = 150% ROAS (get $1.50 back per $1 spent). Valid range: 0.01 to 1000.0. Requires optimization_goal=VALUE.

REQUIRED on the parent ad set for any creative built with multi-variant copy (messages / headlines / descriptions arrays in CreativeSpec). Note: dynamic-creative ad sets accept only ONE ad. Defaults to false.

tool.name: get_pixel_health
tool.title: Get Pixel Health
tool.description:
Get pixel health for a Meta ad account — metadata, event counts, source and host breakdown.

Returns the account's pixel(s) with:
- Metadata: name, last_fired_time, automatic matching config, first-party cookie status
- Event stats (last 7 days): per-event counts (PageView, Purchase, AddToCart, etc.)
- Source breakdown (last 7 days): browser pixel vs Conversions API (CAPI) event counts
- Host breakdown (last 7 days): which domains/sites the pixel fires on

Use this to diagnose tracking issues: missing events, low CAPI coverage, stale pixels,
or disabled automatic advanced matching.

The pixels array from list_ad_accounts provides basic info (id, name, last_fired_time).
Use this tool for the full diagnostic breakdown.

outputSchema.description: Per-pixel health snapshot for an ad account.

pixels.description: Per-pixel summary: id, name, last_fired_time, code (Meta health code), events_by_type (PageView, Purchase, etc.) and events_by_source (browser, server/CAPI). Use to diagnose tracking gaps.

tool.name: list_creatives
tool.title: List Ad Creatives
tool.description:
List existing ad creatives for an account — use to find a creative_id for reuse with create_ad.

Queries the tenant DB directly — fast indexed query, no metrics aggregation.
Returns id, name, status, object_type, body (truncated unless creative_ids
is set), headline, call_to_action_type, link_url, url_tags, image_hash,
video_id, actor_id (page_id), instagram_user_id, effective_object_story_id,
and lead_gen_form_id.

lead_gen_form_id is the Meta Lead Form this creative collects leads into
(null for non-lead ads). It answers "which form does this ad use?" — pass
it to get_lead_form to see the actual questions. Carousels can point
different cards at different forms, so lead_gen_form_ids holds all of them
and lead_gen_form_id is the first.

Pagination: response includes total / count / offset / has_more / next_offset.
When has_more is true, call again with offset=next_offset to fetch the next page.

Typical workflow (reuse existing creative):
1. list_creatives(account_id) — find existing creative_id
2. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}]) — attach to ad set

Resolving what an ad runs:
1. list_ads(account_id) — read creative.id off the ad
2. list_creatives(account_id, creative_ids=['<that id>'])

search.description: Filter by name (case-insensitive substring match). Omit to browse most recent.

object_type.description: Filter by object_type: IMAGE, VIDEO, SHARE, etc. Omit for all types.

creative_ids.description: Look up specific creatives by id — e.g. the creative.id returned by list_ads, so you can resolve what an ad is actually running. When set, the full (untruncated) body and the raw object_story_spec / call_to_action are returned as well.

limit.description: Max results to return per page (default 25, max 100).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Use next_offset from a prior response to fetch the next page.

anyOf.description: Response from list_creatives.

total.description: Total matching rows across all pages.

count.description: Number of rows in this response.

has_more.description: True when there are more rows past this page.

next_offset.description: Pass to the next call's offset parameter (null when has_more is false).

total_unfiltered.description: How many creatives exist in scope before discretionary filtering. Zero means the scope genuinely has none; non-zero with an empty result means the filters excluded them all. Creatives sync every ~30 min — very recent ones may lag.

message.description: Set when the result page is empty but rows exist — explains what the filters excluded. Relay it rather than concluding the entity is missing.

items.description: One creative row from list_creatives.

body.description: Primary ad text. Truncated to 100 chars when browsing; full text when the creative was requested by id via creative_ids.

url_tags.description: URL parameters appended to the destination link.

instagram_user_id.description: Instagram identity used by this creative, if any.

effective_object_story_id.description: The underlying Page post ({page_id}_{post_id}), for post-backed creatives.

lead_gen_form_id.description: The Meta Lead Form this creative collects leads into, or null for non-lead ads. Pass it to get_lead_form to see the form's questions.

lead_gen_form_ids.description: Every lead form referenced by this creative. Normally one; a carousel can point different cards at different forms.

object_story_spec.description: Raw Meta creative spec — returned only when creative_ids was supplied.

call_to_action.description: Raw top-level CTA — returned only when creative_ids was supplied.

anyOf.description:
Where an account-data answer came from and as of when.

Every read served by the Meta Ads Data Service carries this. The row shape
never depends on the source — only this block does. A read the service
cannot answer for an account whose first sync has not completed (history
beyond the live window, too many entities) is answered with
``{"status": "not_yet_landed", "message", "sync_state", ...}`` instead of
the tool's normal payload; ``{"status": "live_read_unavailable",
"retry_after"}`` means Meta could not be read right now — retry later.
Those two payloads are ``NotYetLandedResponse`` and
``LiveReadUnavailableResponse`` below, and a tool that can answer with
them declares it through ``Refusable[...]``.

source.description: 'mirror' = the synced copy (refreshed every ~30 min); 'live' = read from Meta just now because the account's first sync has not completed; 'live_only' = data Meta alone holds.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the data is current as of.

stale_reason.description: Set when the synced copy can no longer advance: 'token_invalid' (reconnect Meta) or 'disconnected'. Null when healthy.

provenance.description: Source and freshness of this answer.

anyOf.description:
What a façade-backed tool answers instead of its normal payload when
the account's first sync has not completed and the question is outside
what a Live Read may answer — ``NotYetLanded.to_mcp()`` field for field.
A normal result, never ``isError``: relay ``message`` and, when asked how
far along the sync is, ``sync_state``.

message.description: One sentence to relay: what is available until the sync completes and why this request needs more.

live_window_days.description: Days of insights history a Live Read answers (the live window).

anyOf.description:
Progress of an account's first sync — ``SyncState.as_dict()``
(``app.services.meta_ads_data.landed``) field for field.

landed.description: True once every stream of the first sync has completed.

phase.description: initial | catchup | landed | failed; null without a sync record.

basis.description: What the verdict rests on: 'run' (a sync record), 'legacy' (the data_synced flag) or 'none'.

streams.description: Per-stream status: pending | running | completed | failed.

insights_chunks.description: {done, total} chunks of the insights backfill.

sync_state.description: How far the first sync is.

anyOf.description:
Meta could not be read for the account right now (throttled, time
budget exceeded) — ``LiveReadUnavailable.to_mcp()`` field for field.
A normal result, never ``isError``; retry after ``retry_after`` seconds.

tool.name: create_creative
tool.title: Create Ad Creative
tool.description:
Create one or more Meta ad creatives. NOT idempotent — each call creates new creatives.

Pass a list of ``creatives`` to create several in a single tool call (e.g.
five image variants for A/B testing, or one creative per hash returned by
the multi-select asset picker). Each item is processed independently and
an error on one does not abort the others — inspect the per-item
``status`` in the returned ``results`` list.

Batching rule of thumb: if you have N image_hashes / video_ids in hand
from one picker turn, make ONE create_creative call with N items in
``creatives``. Calling this tool N times is wasteful and counts against
the user's quota.

Supports three formats per item:
- image_link: single image link ad (requires image_hash + link)
- video: video ad (requires video_id only — the thumbnail is resolved
  server-side from the video at create time. If Meta is still
  processing the video, the item fails with a wait-and-retry error.
  To pin a custom thumbnail, pass thumbnail_image_hash.)
- existing_post: promote an existing FB/IG post (requires object_story_id)

PLACEMENT ASSET CUSTOMIZATION: when the user has multiple aspect-ratio
cuts of the SAME ad concept (1:1 for Feed, 9:16 for Stories, 16:9 for
video feeds), build ONE creative with placement_videos /
placement_images mapping each cut to its placement_groups — never one
creative per cut. One asset must carry the DEFAULT group (catch-all,
also covers Reels). The parent ad set must NOT be dynamic-creative.
Different concepts/hooks still get separate creatives.

page_id is auto-resolved per account — do NOT ask the user for it.
For video format: do NOT pass thumbnail_url and do NOT ask the user to
pick a thumbnail — the server resolves a fresh one from the video.
thumbnail_url values from search_ad_videos results are signed CDN
links that expire; they are discarded and re-resolved server-side.

Typical full workflow (multi-variant):
1. search_ad_images / search_ad_videos — user picks up to 10 assets
2. create_creative(account_id, creatives=[{...}, {...}, ...]) — one item per asset
3. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}, ...])

IMAGE HASH PROVENANCE RULE. Every ``image_hash`` you pass MUST originate
from one of these in the current conversation:
  - a ``search_ad_images`` result (the user selected it from the picker, or
    the tool returned it for a query you ran), OR
  - a ``complete_upload`` response (``results[].image_hash``).

Do NOT reuse hashes from prior conversations or from training context. If
you have a hash you're unsure about, call
``search_ad_images(account_id, queries=['<hash>'])`` first to confirm it
exists in this account before passing it here. Skipping this rule is the
single biggest cause of the wrong creative ending up on the wrong ad.

Common Meta API errors (per item):
- "Invalid image hash" — re-upload the image or verify image_hash with search_ad_images
- "Invalid OAuth token" / code 190 — user must reconnect their Meta account
- "Permission denied" / code 200 — check ad account permissions

creatives.description:
One or more creative specifications. Pass a list with one element for a single creative, or many for a batch.

ALWAYS BATCH when the user picks multiple assets in the same picker turn. The asset picker (search_ad_images / search_ad_videos) supports multi-select up to 10 — when the user selects N hashes/video_ids, build N CreativeSpecs and pass them all in a single create_creative call. Do NOT call create_creative once per hash; that wastes the user's tool quota.

Each item is processed independently; a failure on one does not abort the others (inspect per-item ``status`` in the returned ``results``).

Three formats supported per item:
- format='video': requires video_id only. The thumbnail is resolved server-side from the video at create time — do NOT copy thumbnail_url values from search_ad_videos results (signed CDN links that expire; they are discarded and re-resolved anyway). To pin a custom thumbnail, pass thumbnail_image_hash.
- format='image_link': requires image_hash and link
- format='existing_post': requires object_story_id OR instagram_post_url OR facebook_post_url

MULTIPLE ASPECT RATIOS OF THE SAME CONCEPT (e.g. the user uploaded 1:1 + 9:16 + 16:9 cuts of one ad): build ONE creative with placement_videos (or placement_images) mapping each cut to its placements — do NOT create one creative per cut, that fragments delivery into separate ads. Example: placement_videos=[{video_id: '<1x1>', placement_groups: ['FEED']}, {video_id: '<9x16>', placement_groups: ['STORY']}, {video_id: '<16x9>', placement_groups: ['DEFAULT']}]. Requires link; exactly one asset must carry DEFAULT (the catch-all, also covers Reels). Distinct concepts/hooks still get separate creatives — placement assets are for cuts of the SAME concept.
Optional copy fields: message, headline, description, call_to_action_type, url_tags.
For multi-variant copy on a single creative: use messages[], headlines[], descriptions[] (max 5 each).
For lead-generation ads: set lead_gen_form_id (create the form in Meta Ads Manager, or via list_lead_forms / create_lead_form when enabled). The tool auto-substitutes the placeholder link 'http://fb.me/' and embeds the form ID in call_to_action.value — required for any ad set whose optimization_goal is LEAD_GENERATION/QUALITY_LEAD with destination_type=ON_AD.
page_id is auto-resolved — do NOT ask the user for it.

items.description:
Specification for creating a Meta ad creative.

Supports image_link, video, carousel, and existing_post formats.
Multi-variant copy (asset_feed_spec) is supported via messages/headlines/descriptions arrays.

format.description: Creative format: 'image_link' (static image ad), 'video' (video ad), 'carousel' (2-10 swipeable cards, each with its own asset and destination), or 'existing_post' (promote an existing Facebook post).

name.description: Creative name in the account's creative library. Strongly recommended: list_creatives can only be searched by name, so an unnamed creative is effectively unfindable afterwards.

phone_number.description: Business phone number in E.164 form, e.g. '+15551234567'. REQUIRED when call_to_action_type='CALL_NOW' (call ads) and rejected otherwise. The MCP emits Meta's documented call_to_action.value = {'link': 'tel:<number>'} shape. Pair with an ad set using destination_type='PHONE_CALL', optimization_goal='QUALITY_CALL', device_platforms=['mobile'] and publisher_platforms=['facebook'].

items.description:
One card in a carousel creative.

Each card is its own image or video with its own headline, description and
destination — that is what makes carousels worth using over a single image.

video_id.description: Video ID from upload_ad_video / search_ad_videos. A video card must ALSO set image_hash as its thumbnail — Meta requires one alongside child_attachments.video_id.

link.description: Destination for this card. Required unless the creative sets lead_gen_form_id (lead carousels use Meta's fb.me placeholder).

call_to_action_type.description: Per-card CTA. Defaults to the creative-level call_to_action_type.

carousel_cards.description: Cards for format='carousel'. Meta allows 2-10. With lead_gen_form_id set, every card points at that same form — Meta does not support different forms per card.

image_hash.description: Image hash from upload_ad_image or search_ad_images. Required for image_link format.

link.description: Destination URL for the ad (e.g. 'https://example.com/shop'). Required for image_link format unless lead_gen_form_id is set (lead-form creatives use 'http://fb.me/' automatically). Optional for video (omit for awareness-only video).

lead_gen_form_id.description: Meta Lead Form ID to attach to the creative — get one from list_lead_forms, create one with create_lead_form, or create it in Meta Ads Manager. Required when the parent ad set is configured for lead generation (optimization_goal=LEAD_GENERATION/QUALITY_LEAD with destination_type=ON_AD). When set: the link is auto-overridden to 'http://fb.me/', and call_to_action.value embeds the form ID. The CTA type must be one of APPLY_NOW, DOWNLOAD, GET_QUOTE, LEARN_MORE, SIGN_UP, or SUBSCRIBE (defaults to SIGN_UP). Works with image_link, video, carousel (every card gets the same form — Meta allows only one per carousel) and existing_post (the form rides on a top-level call_to_action, since a boosted post has no object_story_spec).

video_id.description: Video ID from search_ad_videos. Required for video format.

thumbnail_image_hash.description: OPTIONAL image hash to pin as the video thumbnail (from upload_ad_image or search_ad_images). Omit to let the server resolve the video's processed thumbnail at create time (recommended). Provide this OR thumbnail_url (not both).

thumbnail_url.description: OPTIONAL custom thumbnail URL — only for a stable, publicly hosted image (e.g. your own CDN). Do NOT copy thumbnail_url values from search_ad_videos results: those are signed Meta CDN links that expire within minutes, so they are discarded and re-resolved server-side anyway. Omit to let the server resolve the video's processed thumbnail at create time (recommended). Provide this OR thumbnail_image_hash (not both).

items.description: One video mapped to the placement groups it should serve.

placement_groups.description: Placement group(s) this video serves. Match the asset's aspect ratio to the placement: FEED for 1:1/4:5, STORY for 9:16, VIDEO_FEEDS for 16:9. Use DEFAULT on exactly one asset as the catch-all for every placement not claimed by another asset (including Reels).

placement_videos.description: PLACEMENT ASSET CUSTOMIZATION (format='video' only): serve a different video per placement from ONE creative — e.g. the 1:1 cut in Feed, the 9:16 cut in Stories, the 16:9 cut in video feeds — instead of creating one ad per aspect ratio. Pass 2-10 entries, each {video_id, placement_groups}. Mark exactly one entry DEFAULT as the catch-all. Mutually exclusive with video_id, thumbnail fields, and multi-variant copy (messages/headlines/descriptions). Requires 'link'. The parent ad set must have is_dynamic_creative=false (the default). Thumbnails are resolved server-side per video. When a user has uploaded multiple aspect-ratio cuts of the SAME concept, use this — do NOT create one creative per cut.

items.description: One image mapped to the placement groups it should serve.

placement_groups.description: Placement group(s) this image serves. Match the asset's aspect ratio to the placement: FEED for 1:1/4:5, STORY for 9:16. Use DEFAULT on exactly one asset as the catch-all for every placement not claimed by another asset.

placement_images.description: PLACEMENT ASSET CUSTOMIZATION (format='image_link' only): serve a different image per placement from ONE creative. Pass 2-10 entries, each {image_hash, placement_groups}. Mark exactly one entry DEFAULT as the catch-all. Mutually exclusive with image_hash and multi-variant copy. Requires 'link'. The parent ad set must have is_dynamic_creative=false (the default). When a user has uploaded multiple aspect-ratio cuts of the SAME concept, use this — do NOT create one creative per cut.

object_story_id.description: Existing Facebook post ID in the format '<PAGE_ID>_<POST_ID>'. For existing_post format. Provide this OR instagram_post_url OR facebook_post_url.

instagram_post_url.description: Instagram post URL (e.g. 'https://www.instagram.com/p/DVb6nP5Cbm7/'). For existing_post format. Auto-resolved to the Instagram media ID. Provide this OR object_story_id OR facebook_post_url.

facebook_post_url.description: Facebook post URL (e.g. share link, permalink, or /posts/ URL). For existing_post format. Auto-resolved to object_story_id. Provide this OR object_story_id OR instagram_post_url.

message.description: Primary ad text (body copy) shown above the image/video. Mutually exclusive with 'messages' (multi-variant).

headline.description: Headline text. For image_link: shown below the image in the link preview. For video: mapped to video_data.title. Mutually exclusive with 'headlines' (multi-variant).

description.description: Description text shown below the headline in the link preview. Mutually exclusive with 'descriptions' (multi-variant).

messages.description: Multiple body copy variants (up to 5). Meta optimizes which variant to show per viewer. Produces asset_feed_spec instead of inline copy. Requires a dynamic creative ad set (is_dynamic_creative=true). Mutually exclusive with 'message'.

headlines.description: Multiple headline variants (up to 5). Meta optimizes which to show per viewer. Mutually exclusive with 'headline'.

descriptions.description: Multiple description variants (up to 5). Meta optimizes which to show per viewer. Mutually exclusive with 'description'.

page_id.description: Facebook Page ID to post the ad from. Omit to auto-resolve from existing creatives on this account.

instagram_user_id.description: Instagram account ID for Instagram placement (optional).

call_to_action_type.description: Call-to-action button label, e.g. 'SHOP_NOW', 'LEARN_MORE', 'SIGN_UP', 'GET_OFFER'. Omit to use Meta's default.

url_tags.description: UTM tracking parameters appended to the link URL, e.g. 'utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=paid'.

agent_intent.description: OPTIONAL free-text describing why the agent is creating these creatives (e.g. '5-variant hook test for new BFCM angle'). Logged for telemetry.

outputSchema.description: Result of create_creative — N creatives created (interleaved results).

next_steps.description: Recommended follow-up tool call(s) for the LLM. Required on every successful mutation per CLAUDE.md; left Optional here because some tools (e.g. update_entity) currently omit it.

creative_ids.description: IDs of successfully-created creatives. Pass these to create_ad.

results.description: Per-creative results — one entry per input spec.

items.description:
Per-creative result inside create_creative.results.

Unlike other batch creation tools, create_creative interleaves successes
and errors in a single `results` list. Inspect each item's `status`.

format.description: Creative format that was built (image_link, video, existing_post, etc.).

detail.description: Raw exception string for debugging. May leak stack-trace context.

tool.name: create_ad
tool.title: Create Ad
tool.description:
Create one or more ads by attaching creatives to ad sets.

NOT idempotent — each call creates new ads.

Typical workflow:
1. search_ad_images / search_ad_videos — find an asset
2. create_creative(account_id, creatives=[creative_spec]) — build creatives → creative_ids
3. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}]) — create this tool

Shortcut (reuse existing creative):
1. list_creatives(account_id) — find an existing creative_id
2. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}])

All ads are created as PAUSED by default. Activate with change_entity_status.
Accepts a list to support A/B testing (multiple creatives, same ad set).

Conversion-tracked campaigns (OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_LEADS via website) MUST
set conversion_domain to the registrable domain of the destination URL
(e.g. 'example.com', not 'https://shop.example.com/path'). Meta rejects
otherwise with subcode 2490408 ('Missing conversion domain'). Skip for
awareness/engagement campaigns and lead-form (instant form) ads.

Common errors:
- Invalid creative_id: verify with list_creatives or create a new one
- Invalid adset_id: verify with list_adsets
- 'Missing conversion domain' / subcode 2490408: pass conversion_domain
- OAuthException / token expiry: ask user to reconnect their Meta account
- Permission error: app may lack ad_management permission

ads.description: One or more ad specs to create. Each attaches a creative to an ad set.

items.description: Specification for creating a single Meta ad.

name.description: Display name for the ad (shown in Ads Manager).

adset_id.description: Ad set ID to attach this ad to (from list_adsets).

creative_id.description: Creative ID to use for this ad. Obtain via create_creative or list_creatives.

status.description: Initial status. Locked to PAUSED to enforce the AdAdvisor policy that all newly-created ads must be reviewed before going live. Activate explicitly after review with change_entity_status(action='resume').

conversion_domain.description: Second-level domain (e.g. 'example.com', NOT 'https://shop.example.com/path') where conversions are recorded. REQUIRED by Meta for any ad in a campaign that shares data with a pixel — Meta returns subcode 2490408 ('Missing conversion domain') if omitted. Set to the registrable domain of the creative's destination URL: e.g. for a creative linking to https://shop.example.com/checkout, pass conversion_domain='example.com'. Optional for awareness/engagement campaigns and lead-form ads (which use Meta's hosted form, not a tracked website).

agent_intent.description: OPTIONAL free-text describing why the agent is creating these ads (e.g. 'wiring 5 new creatives into the BOFU retargeting ad set'). Logged for telemetry.

outputSchema.description: Result of create_ad — N ads created (all PAUSED unless overridden).

next_steps.description: Recommended follow-up tool call(s) for the LLM. Required on every successful mutation per CLAUDE.md; left Optional here because some tools (e.g. update_entity) currently omit it.

all_succeeded.description: True if every item succeeded (no entries in `errors`).

errors.description: Per-item failure records. Each carries `name` plus the keys from format_tool_error() (`error`, `exception_type`, `meta_error?`, `hint?`). Present when error_count > 0.

ads.description: Per-ad records on success. Note: field name is `ads` (not `created`).

items.description: Successfully-created ad in a create_ad batch response.

status.description: Initial status — PAUSED unless caller overrode.

conversion_domain.description: The verified domain attached to this ad (required by Meta on conversion-tracked ads).

warnings.description: Non-fatal configuration problems found before the write — most often a lead-gen mismatch between the creative and its ad set. The ads WERE created (PAUSED); resolve these before resuming them, or they will run without collecting leads.

tool.name: list_lead_forms
tool.title: List Lead Forms
tool.description:
List existing Meta Lead Forms (instant forms) for a Facebook Page.

Lead forms are page-scoped (endpoint: /{page_id}/leadgen_forms), so the
tool resolves a Page first. If page_id is omitted, the account's default
promote_page is used — call list_pages first when the account has
multiple Pages and you need a different one.

Returns id, name, status, locale, leads_count, follow_up_action_url,
question count, and privacy_policy_url for each form. Use the form
id as lead_gen_form_id in create_creative to attach to a new ad.

Calls Meta directly — lead forms are not ingested into the tenant DB.

Common workflow (reuse existing form):
1. list_lead_forms(account_id, status='ACTIVE') — find an active form
2. get_lead_form(account_id, lead_form_id) — check what it asks
3. create_creative(creatives=[{format:'image_link', image_hash:'...',
                               lead_gen_form_id:'<form_id>'}])
4. create_adset(..., optimization_goal='LEAD_GENERATION',
                destination_type='ON_AD',
                promoted_object={'page_id': '<this Page>'})
   promoted_object is REQUIRED on an OUTCOME_LEADS ad set.

Requires the token to have ads_management + pages_show_list. Read
access to submitted leads additionally requires MANAGE_LEADS on the
page (use list_pages to verify task grants), and is what list_leads
needs.

page_id.description: Facebook Page ID to query. Omit to use the account's default promote_page (the same page create_lead_form picks). Call list_pages if the account has more than one page and you need to pin a specific one.

search.description: Filter by form name (case-insensitive substring match). Omit to return all.

status.description: Filter by form status. Omit for all statuses. Only ACTIVE forms can be attached to new ads — ARCHIVED forms will be rejected at ad creation.

limit.description: Max results to return per page (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Use next_offset from a prior response to fetch the next page.

outputSchema.description: Response from list_lead_forms.

total.description: Total matching rows across all pages.

count.description: Number of rows in this response.

has_more.description: True when there are more rows past this page.

next_offset.description: Pass to the next call's offset parameter (null when has_more is false).

page_id.description: Facebook Page the forms were queried from.

page_name.description: Display name of the queried Page.

total_unfiltered.description: How many forms the Page has before `search`/`status` filtering. A zero here means the Page genuinely has no forms; a non-zero with an empty result means the filters excluded them all.

items.description: One lead form row from list_lead_forms.

id.description: Lead form ID (use as lead_gen_form_id in create_creative).

status.description: ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DELETED, or DRAFT. Only ACTIVE forms can be used in new ads.

expired_leads_count.description: Leads that have aged past Meta's 90-day retrieval window.

block_display_for_non_targeted_viewer.description: True when the form blocks organic / non-targeted submissions.

questions_count.description: Number of questions in the form.

question_types.description: Question types in display order, e.g. ['FULL_NAME','EMAIL','CUSTOM']. Call get_lead_form for the full labels, options and disclaimers.

tool.name: get_lead_form
tool.title: Get Lead Form
tool.description:
Inspect one Meta Lead Form in full — every question, disclaimer and screen.

Use this whenever you need to know what a form actually ASKS. A lead
form's questions CANNOT be edited after creation, so reading an existing
form is the only way to judge whether it fits a campaign — and the only
way to decide whether to reuse it or build a new one.

Returns the complete form: questions (type, key, label, dropdown options,
helper text), the intro context_card, the thank_you_page, legal_content
(custom consent checkboxes), privacy_policy_url, tracking_parameters,
follow_up_action_url, the quality/gating flags, and lifetime lead counts.

`questions[].key` is the field name that appears in the submitted lead
payload — match on it when mapping a form to a CRM.

Typical uses:
- "Which form does this ad use, and what does it ask?" — read
  lead_gen_form_id from list_creatives, then call this.
- Before reusing a form: confirm the questions suit the new offer.
- Diagnosing low lead quality: too few questions, or no
  is_optimized_for_quality.

Calls Meta directly (lead forms are not ingested into the tenant DB) and
needs a Page access token, so the connected user must have a role on the
owning Page.

lead_form_id.description: Lead form ID — from list_lead_forms, from create_lead_form's response, or from a creative's lead_gen_form_id (list_creatives).

page_id.description: Facebook Page that owns the form. Omit to use the account's default promote_page. Only needed when the account has several Pages and the form lives on a non-default one (see list_pages).

outputSchema.description:
Full detail for a single lead form, from get_lead_form.

A lead form's questions cannot be edited after creation, so this read is
the only way to inspect what an in-market form actually asks.

status.description: ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DELETED, or DRAFT.

questions.description: Every question on the form, in display order.

items.description: One question as Meta stores it on an existing lead form.

type.description: Question type, e.g. EMAIL, PHONE, FULL_NAME, CUSTOM. Non-CUSTOM types are prefilled by Meta from the user's profile.

key.description: Stable field key — this is the name that appears in the lead payload.

label.description: Question text shown to the user.

options.description: Dropdown choices for CUSTOM questions, as [{key, value}].

inline_context.description: Helper text shown beneath the question.

context_card.description: The intro screen shown before the questions (title, style, content, button_text).

thank_you_page.description: The completion screen shown after submission.

legal_content.description: Custom disclaimers / consent checkboxes attached to the form.

tracking_parameters.description: Flat key/value map echoed back on every lead for this form.

allow_organic_lead.description: True when the form can also be submitted from organic (non-ad) traffic.

is_optimized_for_quality.description: True for the higher-intent form type (adds a review step before submit). Trades volume for lead quality.

leads_count.description: Total leads collected to date (all time, not date-scoped).

expired_leads_count.description: Leads that have aged past Meta's 90-day retrieval window.

tool.name: check_lead_gen_readiness
tool.title: Check Lead-Gen Readiness
tool.description:
Check whether this account can actually run lead gen — BEFORE building anything.

Lead generation has four independent prerequisites, and each one fails
at a different point with a different, unhelpful Meta error. Run this
first and you learn all four at once instead of discovering them one
campaign at a time:

1. A Facebook Page the account can advertise from.
2. ads_management + pages_manage_ads on the token — to create forms
   and lead ad sets.
3. leads_retrieval + lead access on the Page — to read the leads back.
   A token can have everything else and still not be able to see a
   single lead.
4. The Page owner has accepted Meta's Lead Ads Terms of Service, at
   https://www.facebook.com/ads/leadgen/tos — this one is not
   grantable through OAuth and must be done by a Page admin.

Returns can_create_forms / can_retrieve_leads plus a `blockers` list
naming what to do about each. Call it before create_lead_form when a
user is setting up lead gen for the first time, or whenever a lead
tool returns a permission error.

page_id.description: Page to check. Omit to use the account's default promote_page.

outputSchema.description: Readiness verdict for lead generation on one ad account + Page.

leadgen_tos_accepted.description: Whether the Page has accepted Meta's Lead Generation Terms of Service. null = could not be determined (treat as unknown, NOT as false). False blocks every lead-ads write for the Page until a Page admin accepts at https://www.facebook.com/ads/leadgen/tos.

granted_scopes.description: null means the permission lookup failed — unknown, not empty.

items.description: One prerequisite currently failing, with what to do about it.

reason.description: Machine key: no_page | no_page_token | no_advertise_task | no_manage_leads_task | missing_scopes | leadgen_tos_not_accepted | lead_retrieval_not_available

detail.description: What is wrong, in plain English.

user_action.description: What the human must do to clear it.

note.description: Advisory caveats about interpreting this verdict.

error.description: Degraded-read detail from the Page listing, if any.

next_steps.description: Suggested next tool calls when fully ready.

tool.name: create_lead_form_audience
tool.title: Create Lead-Form Audience
tool.description:
Build a custom audience from how people interacted with a lead form.

This is what turns lead gen into a funnel instead of a one-shot: the
people who opened your form and didn't finish are the warmest audience
the campaign creates, and submitters should usually be EXCLUDED from
prospecting so you stop paying to re-acquire them.

NOT idempotent — each call creates a new audience.

Audiences take a few hours to populate and need ~1000 people before
Meta will deliver against them.

Typical uses:
- Retarget drop-offs: event_name='lead_generation_dropoff'
- Exclude existing leads: event_name='lead_generation_submitted', then
  pass the audience to update_adset_targeting as an exclusion
- Seed a lookalike: create with 'lead_generation_submitted', then
  create_lookalike_audience from it

name.description: Audience name, e.g. 'Form openers - not submitted - 30d'.

form_ids.description: Lead form IDs to build the audience from (list_lead_forms).

event_name.description: Which interaction to capture. lead_generation_submitted = completed the form (EXCLUDE these from prospecting so you stop paying for leads you already have; use as a lookalike seed). lead_generation_opened = opened it. lead_generation_dropoff = opened but did not submit — the highest-intent retargeting pool a lead campaign produces.

retention_days.description: How long someone stays in the audience. Meta caps lead-form engagement audiences at 90 days (unlike Page or site audiences).

source.description: Which surface the form was filled on. Instagram lead forms are a separate event source from Facebook ones.

description.description: Optional note stored on the audience.

outputSchema.description:
Result of create_lead_form_audience — lead-form engagement audience.

Deliberately its own model rather than reusing the website one: a
lead-form audience has no pixel and no prefill, so annotating the tool
with CreateWebsiteAudienceResponse made FastMCP's output validation fail
on the missing `event_name`/`pixel_id`/`prefill` — AFTER the audience had
already been created on Meta. The caller saw an error for a mutation that
had succeeded, which invites a retry and a duplicate audience.

operation_status.description: Meta's operation_status object for population state (None until ready).

approximate_count_lower_bound.description: Lower bound of approximate audience size. None until Meta finishes populating.

event_name.description: Which form interaction the audience captures.

form_ids.description: Lead forms the audience was built from.

retention_days.description: How long someone stays in the audience (Meta caps this at 90).

source.description: 'facebook' or 'instagram' — which surface the form was filled on.

tool.name: set_lead_form_status
tool.title: Archive / Reactivate Lead Form
tool.description:
Archive or reactivate a Meta Lead Form.

Archiving is the ONLY retirement path Meta offers — lead forms cannot be
deleted, by us or by anyone. Status is also the only property of a form
that can ever be changed after creation; questions, disclaimers and
screens are immutable, so a form with the wrong questions must be
archived and replaced.

Archiving a form that live ads still point at will stop those ads
collecting leads. Check first with list_creatives (read lead_gen_form_id)
before archiving anything in use.

Idempotent — setting a status the form already has is a no-op that
returns success.

lead_form_id.description: Lead form ID, from list_lead_forms or create_lead_form.

status.description: ARCHIVED retires the form: it stops accepting new submissions and cannot be attached to new ads. ACTIVE restores it. Already-collected leads are NOT affected.

page_id.description: Facebook Page that owns the form. Omit to use the account's default promote_page.

outputSchema.description: Result of set_lead_form_status.

status.description: Literal 'success'.

lead_form_status.description: The form's status after the change (ACTIVE or ARCHIVED).

previous_status.description: The form's status before the change.

update_id.description: entity_updates audit row id for this change.

tool.name: create_lead_form
tool.title: Create Lead Form(s)
tool.description:
Create one or more Meta Lead Forms (instant forms) on a Facebook Page.

NOT idempotent — each call creates new forms. Forms cannot be deleted,
only ARCHIVED, so prefer one well-tested form over many trial forms.

Lead forms are page-scoped: the create endpoint is /{page_id}/leadgen_forms.
If page_id is omitted on a spec, the service auto-resolves the first
promote_pages entry for the account. Call list_pages first if the
account has multiple pages and you need to pin a specific one.

REQUIRED fields per spec: name, questions, privacy_policy (url + link_text),
and follow_up_action_url. The follow_up_action_url is enforced by Meta
even though it isn't documented in the public Marketing API guide —
omitting it returns 'Missing field(s): FollowUpActionURL'.

Use these forms in a creative by passing the form ID directly:
  create_creative(creatives=[{format:'image_link', image_hash:'...',
                               lead_gen_form_id:'<form_id>'}])
The MCP layer auto-substitutes the placeholder link 'http://fb.me/' and
embeds the form ID in call_to_action.value as Meta requires. CTA defaults

tool.name: upload_creatives
tool.title: Upload Creatives
tool.description:
Open the upload widget for adding images and videos to a Meta ad account.

Opens an interactive widget where the user can:
- Drag & drop or browse for image files (JPG, PNG, max 30 MB) and videos (MP4, MOV, max 4 GB)
- Paste URLs to images or videos (MP4, MOV) for upload
- Upload multiple files at once with per-item progress

After upload, the image hashes and video IDs are sent back automatically
so they can be used with create_creative and create_ad.

This tool validates the account and access token before opening the widget.
If the token has expired, ask the user to reconnect their Meta account.

the full S3 → Meta flow. This tool returns presigned PUT URLs for each
file; the widget uploads directly to S3 using these URLs, then calls

image hashes and video IDs.

tool.name: search_ad_images
tool.title: Search Ad Images
tool.description:
Search images in this account's ad library and open a visual picker to select one or more.

Queries meta_ad_images by name (case-insensitive) OR by exact hash, fetches
fresh thumbnail URLs from Meta API, then opens the asset picker widget. The
user can select up to 10 images at once, then clicks Confirm — the chosen
image_hashes are sent back to Claude in a single ``updateModelContext``
payload (numbered list when multiple).

Each query string is matched as a HASH if it's a 32-character hex string;
otherwise it's matched as a case-insensitive substring against the image
name. This lets you confirm a hash you got from ``complete_upload`` exists
in cache: ``queries=['9f07e04cb9ec2dcefee32ae9eca9cce7']``.

Pass several keywords at once with ``queries=[...]`` to search a batch of
terms in a single call. Each returned image carries ``matched_queries`` so
you can see which term(s) it matched.

Read ``unmatched_queries`` in the response. Any term in that list returned
ZERO images. Do NOT substitute an unrelated image from ``images`` for an
unmatched query — that's how the wrong creative ends up on the wrong ad.

If the user just uploaded images via ``init_upload``/``complete_upload`` in
this conversation, the ``image_hash`` values from that response are
authoritative — pass them directly to ``create_creative`` instead of
re-searching by name.

Multi-select workflow (recommended for multi-variant creatives):
1. search_ad_images(account_id, queries=['Royal Blue', 'Indigo', 'Navy']) — user picks several hashes in one go
2. create_creative(account_id, creatives=[{format: 'image_link', image_hash: '<h1>', ...}, {format: 'image_link', image_hash: '<h2>', ...}, ...])
   ↑ Pass ALL the selected hashes in a single batched call — do NOT call create_creative once per hash.
3. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}, ...])

Single-select workflow (one creative):
1. search_ad_images(account_id, queries=['green watch']) — user picks one image
2. create_creative(account_id, creatives=[{format: 'image_link', image_hash: '<hash>', ...}])
3. create_ad(account_id, ads=[{adset_id, creative_id, name}])

Omit queries to browse the most recent images (upload discovery mode).

tool.name: preview_existing_creatives
tool.title: Preview Existing Creatives
tool.description:
Preview existing creatives that use the same image or video, with engagement metrics.

Call this BEFORE creating a new creative to check if the same asset is already
in use. If existing creatives have engagement (reactions, comments, shares),
the user can reuse one via create_ad(creative_id=...) to preserve social proof
instead of creating a new creative (which starts with zero engagement).

Opens a visual preview showing each creative's thumbnail, ad copy, and
engagement counts. The user clicks "Use This Creative" to select one.

Engagement requires a Page access token. When that can't be minted, the
counts come back null with engagement_checked=false and
engagement_available=false — that means UNKNOWN, not zero. Never treat it
as "no social proof" or use it to justify creating a new creative.

Requires either image_hash or video_id (not both).

creatives whose engagement could not be read (engagement_checked=false) are

creative has measured engagement, a `recommendation` string suggests reusing
the top creative; otherwise `message` explains whether engagement was
genuinely zero or simply unreadable.
